record.context_brief: Three-monomial equations with unknown extra solutions
record.original_question: Besides the obvious solutions already known, determine whether the Diophantine equations x^3 y + y z^2 + z = 0 and x + x^3 y + y z^2 = 0 have any other integer solutions.

evidence.quote: The smallest open three-monomial equations are (a) x^3y + yz^2 + z = 0, (b) x + x^2y^2 + z^3 = 0 (13) and x + x^3y + yz^2 = 0. (14)
Equations (13) and (14) are open without any doubts, because they have some obvious solutions, see [1, Section 4.3.5], and it is open whether they have any other solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two Diophantine equations in integer unknowns:

(a) x^3 y + y z^2 + z = 0,
(b) x + x^3 y + y z^2 = 0.

Each equation admits certain "obvious" infinite families of integer solutions (for instance, those obtained by setting one or more variables to 0, e.g. (x,y,z) = (x,0,0) for either equation, and other parametric families that arise by inspection).

Determine, for each of the two equations separately, whether there exist any integer solutions (x, y, z) ∈ ℤ^3 other than these obvious ones. Equivalently, classify completely the set of integer solutions to each equation.
artifact.status_search_result: These equations are listed among the smallest open three-monomial Diophantine equations in current literature on small open Diophantine equations. Recent work develops an algorithm handling many three-monomial equations and maintains an updated list of smallest open cases (including on MathOverflow), but these specific equations remain unresolved as of the most recent available references.
